sources.entry: Homer - Dead simple static homepage to expose your server services, with an easy yaml configuration and connectivity check. (Demo) Apache-2.0 Docker/K8S/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Homer is a static, YAML-configured homepage that gives you a single dashboard of links to the services running on your server.
summary.what_it_does: Homer is a static HTML/JS dashboard generated from a single YAML configuration file (assets/config.yml) that lists your services as cards and groups. It is meant to be served by an HTTP server and will not work when index.html is opened directly via file://. The README lists fuzzy search, multiple pages and item grouping, theme customization, smart cards, and an installable PWA. Keyboard shortcuts let you press / to search, Enter to open the first match, and Alt/Option+Enter to open it in a new tab. Official distribution is a Docker image (b4bz/homer) with bind-mounted config, plus a prebuilt release tarball and a manual pnpm build. The README also mentions a Kubernetes installation section and a connectivity check, though its details are not in the provided text.
use_cases: Build a landing page linking to my self-hosted services
Organize homelab apps into groups and pages
Quick search across my server's web tools
Run a dashboard in Docker or on Kubernetes
Serve a static start page from any web server
Install a dashboard as a PWA on a device
how_to_run: Or with docker-compose: image b4bz/homer, mount /path/to/config/dir to /www/assets, map port 8080
Release tarball: download homer.zip, unzip, cp assets/config.yml.dist assets/config.yml, then serve with pnpx http-server or python -m http.server 8010
notable: Entirely static HTML/JS output driven by one YAML config file, so no backend is needed to serve it
Official Docker image with bind-mounted config, optional subfolder hosting, and configurable port and IPv6 listening
Installable as a PWA with fuzzy search and keyboard shortcuts
Multi-page dashboards with item grouping and theme customization
caveats: Must be served over HTTP; opening index.html directly via file:// does not work
Docker container runs as uid/gid 1000 by default, so the assets directory permissions may need adjusting
